details:
bfvkjmeikpwhqxc 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 (published by the npm account dfghbvbfjh on 2026-10-30, the account's only package) are a cloaked redirector of the kind used for phishing, hosted on npm, not a library: the archive holds only package.json and index.html, and nothing runs at install. index.html imitates a Cloudflare check page ("Just a moment...", "Performing security verification", a generated Ray ID, a Turnstile widget). Its script reads an AES-CTR encrypted value from the public key-value store https://api.keyval.org/get under the key DC7tr9PjVqMIf1EYczH1puouOG21C0khV3VzWnxdtI, decrypts it with a key in the page to get a destination host that appears nowhere in the package, then calls <host>/api/strategies/check?cid=<cid> to decide per target where to send the visitor, and forwards all URL parameters with window.location.replace. The Turnstile callbacks also fire on error, expiry and timeout, so the check gates nothing. The page stays blank unless that check fails, so a visitor it accepts never sees the page at all. Anything on npm can be served through public CDNs, so such a link starts on a trusted host; the destination stays hidden and can change at any time.

Found by Gatekeeper (https://github.com/lb2002/gatekeeper); read statically from the published archives, never executed, and the hidden destination was not looked up.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code

files.note: fake Cloudflare check page that hides its redirect target
